SELECT log_date AS time,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) || ' · RUN → ' || current_status AS title,
       'previous_status = ' || previous_status || ', current_status = ' || current_status AS text,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS tags
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_status_change
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND previous_status = 'RUN'
  AND current_status <> 'RUN'
  AND ('All' IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}) OR equipment_id IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}))
ORDER BY log_date DESC
LIMIT 200;

WITH exits AS (
    SELECT equipment_id, log_date
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_status_change
    WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
      AND previous_status = 'RUN' AND current_status <> 'RUN'
      AND ('All' IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}) OR equipment_id IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}))
)
SELECT a.log_date AS time,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(a.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) || ' · ' || a.error_code AS title,
       a.error_msg AS text,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(a.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS tags
FROM exits e
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    -- the last ALARM-severity trigger in the quarter hour before the machine
    -- left RUN: at most one annotation per exit
    SELECT log_date, error_code, error_msg, equipment_id
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_alarm
    WHERE equipment_id = e.equipment_id
      AND alarm_status = 'Triggered'
      AND error_type = 'ALARM'
      AND log_date <= e.log_date
      AND log_date >= e.log_date - interval '15 minutes'
    ORDER BY log_date DESC
    LIMIT 1
) a
ORDER BY a.log_date DESC
LIMIT 200;

SELECT min(log_date) AS time,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) || ' · ' || jobkey AS title,
       'jobkey = ' || jobkey AS text,
       'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS tags
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND jobkey IS NOT NULL AND jobkey <> ''
  AND ('All' IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}) OR equipment_id IN (${equipment_id:sqlstring}))
GROUP BY 'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2), jobkey
ORDER BY 1 DESC
LIMIT 200;

description:
Operations console for the vertical copper plating (VCP) lines: the latest state of each line, the job being plated, the 7-step bath temperatures, current and voltage of the 18 stations, and the alarm log. Every value is read directly from eap_api_vcp_upp, eap_api_vcp_status_change and eap_api_vcp_alarm.

**Before reading any panel:** a new row lands in `eap_api_vcp_upp` about **once a minute**, so the dashboard can trail the floor by about one minute. `nowDelay` is 1 minute so the right edge of a graph is never a stretch with no data yet. The refresh choices start at 1 minute, because anything shorter re-queries the same rows. **The machines were renamed on 2026-09-11** from `VCP001-VCP` to `VCP01-VCP` (lines 02 and 03 likewise). The "Line" filter therefore selects a physical line, and every panel treats both names as one line; no panel shows an old name as a fourth to sixth line. **Every colour threshold in this folder is tied to an alert rule already in place** or to a property of the data, except where a panel says it is a readability band. A column whose unit the source does not give is shown without a unit. The database is read-only: the `grafana_reader` user cannot write. This dashboard is the operations layer, with a 6-hour default window. The live cards read the newest row of each line at or before the right edge of the time range. For long trends or lot comparisons, go to dashboard 01.

**Basis of the statements in every panel description:** properties checked against the source tables across every machine name they have recorded (`VCP001/002/003-VCP` before the rename, `VCP01/02/03-VCP` after it, and a stray `VCP001-L`). Plant figures such as row counts, setpoints and measured values are deliberately left out of these descriptions.

**Wall display (kiosk):** open `/d/ims-vcp-operations-console?kiosk&_dash.hideTimePicker=true&_dash.hideVariables=true&_dash.hideLinks=true`. Kiosk mode alone still shows the filter, time and link bars (about 105 px), which pushes the bottom of the live panel off a 1080-line screen; with them hidden the whole live panel fits 1920 × 1080. The window stays at the default last 6 hours and refreshes every minute.

panels.description:
**Use it when:** the line is running. This is the line supervisor's main screen: state, job, bath temperatures, the 18 stations of both banks, pumps and alarms of all three lines on one screen.

**How to read it:** plain grey values are where they should be. **Colour appears only where something is off**, so a calm card is a healthy card and the eye goes straight to the exception:

- **amber cell**: a station side more than 5 A from its setpoint, a bath outside its setpoint band, or a pump reading that differs from its setpoint
- **red outlined cell**: a station side at 0 A with a setpoint while the rest of its bank is plating
- **cyan underline**: a side drawing current with no setpoint recorded
- **dash**: a side neither drawing current nor asked to

**Display only.** Nothing on the panel takes a click or an input, and nothing is folded away: every value is on screen. The top bar counts the lines shown by latest `current_status`, how many RUN lines are still sending data, and how many are stale. To show fewer lines, set the `status_filter` variable above the dashboard. The strip below it has five fleet totals.

The panel reads top to bottom in three bands, like a plant overview screen:

1. **Each line at a glance**: one card per line.
   - **Header**: latest `current_status` (coloured pill and top edge), a *test job* tag when `waveform` names a DUMMY job, when the line entered its state, and the age and time of the newest data row.
   - **Hero row**: total `actual_current` of bank a and bank b (never added together) with sides drawing current and their mean voltage, then `line_speed` with `density`, then `jobkey` with `plating_time` and width × height. An empty `jobkey` reads *not recorded*.
   - **Exception chips** stay grey at 0 and fill amber or red above 0:
     - **Off setpoint**: sides more than 5 A from setpoint.
     - **Missing current**: sides at 0 A with a setpoint while the bank plates.
     - **Pumps at 0**: pumps reading 0 with a setpoint.
     - **Open alarms**: codes still open, with how long the oldest has stood.
2. **18 Plating Rectifiers · Side A & B**: one full-width matrix for every line. Columns are stations 01 to 18 in the order the panel travels.
   - Each line has three rows, laid out like the machine: **Side A**, the station setpoint (`preset_current_*`, which side a and side b share on every row), and **Side B**.
   - Every cell gives the current in A (`actual_current_*`) and, beside it, the voltage in V (`actual_voltage_*`, only while the side draws current).
   - **A raised cell is a side drawing current; a dash is idle.** Amber and red appear only for the fault cases in the legend.
   - The name cell says **where the panels are**: the occupied stations as runs (for example *03–08, 13–18*), the cell and group counts, and whether panels are entering at 01 or at the exit at 18.
3. **Details per line**: one card per line.
   - **Pumps**: `actual_pump_1` to `_18`, numbered on their own row. The source does not tie a pump to a station. A pump off its setpoint shows the setpoint beneath the reading in parentheses; when the reading is on setpoint the two are the same number, so it is not repeated.
   - **Bath temperature °C**: the seven flow steps in the order the panel travels (clean, prep, Cu 1, Cu 2, AO, hotwater, dry), then the support baths (heating, peeloff, rectifier). Reading above, setpoint below. `prep` has one column, `actual_prep`, which holds one fixed value per line on every row, so it is the recipe setpoint, not a reading. It sits in the setpoint row; the reading row says n/a and prep is never judged.
   - **Alarms**: the four newest `Triggered` rows in the range and `error_type`, newest first. Each gives time, `error_code` (red text ALARM, amber Warning) and `error_msg`, then either *cleared hh:mm:ss · duration* or *open ≥ duration* with a red left rule. Below them is the most frequent code in the range.
   - **Job record**: `waveform`, `thickness`, `plating_area_a / b`, `frequency_1`, the copper preset current of each side, `copper_thick_low / high` (only when filled), the check-mode codes, `equipment_id` and `factory`.

**How "where the panels are" is known:**
- **The source has no position column.** `preset_tank` and `actual_tank` are empty or 0 on every row, and nothing else records where a panel is.
- **What it does record** is which stations hold a current setpoint and draw current. That set moves down the line at line speed.
  - Followed over time, the band's front reaches station 18 and its tail clears the stations one by one, at a pace set by the line speed.
  - Two bands with a gap between them can travel the line together.
- **So the occupied stations are where panels are.**
- **What the data cannot say:**
  - which group belongs to which job. `jobkey` changes when a new load starts, so a group further down the line can belong to an earlier job;
  - where panels are in clean, prep, AO, hotwater or dry. Those tanks carry no current, so the panel shows them as untracked rather than guessing.

**Calculated from:** the newest `eap_api_vcp_upp` row of each line at or before the right edge of the time range (either name of the line), the latest `eap_api_vcp_status_change` row, and `eap_api_vcp_alarm` filtered by the selected `error_type`, as every other panel on this dashboard is.

**Abnormal when:** a card shows NO DATA or its data age runs into hours, a RUN line has fewer than half its sides plating, or any chip or cell turns amber or red.

**What to do next:** scroll to "Plating Current by Station" and "Cell Voltage by Station" to see how long a station has been off. For a bath, go to "Bath Temperature, 7 Steps", then to dashboard 01 panel "Bath Deviation from Setpoint" for the long trend.

**Stale lines:** a line that has sent nothing for more than 5 minutes before the right edge of the range is **stale**. The data age turns amber, the card's top edge turns grey, and its values dim, because they are the last known readings, not live ones. Fleet current, density, speed and plating sides count only lines still sending data. "RUN with live data" counts lines whose last state is RUN and that are still sending.

**Where the colour limits come from:** every limit on this card is an alert rule already in place, never a number picked for the screen:

| Limit | Alert rule |
| --- | --- |
| Station side 5 A | `vcp-current-deviation-001` |
| Cu 1, Cu 2 and rectifier 4 °C | `vcp-plating-bath-temp-005` |
| Other baths 10 °C | `vcp-support-bath-temp-006` |
| Pump reading not equal to setpoint | `vcp-pump-mismatch-003` |

A bath reading of 0 means no reading and is shown dimmed, not judged.

**Alarms count incidents, not rows:** a code that re-fires on the same machine within 30 minutes is one incident still standing. Most `Triggered` rows re-fire within a few minutes, so counting rows would overstate alarms several times over. **Open** means no `Reset` row of the same `error_code` follows the trigger in the data. Its duration is a minimum, counted up to the newest data row. When the trigger is newer than that row, it shows *open · after the newest data row*. The full log is the "Alarm Log" panel below, and the code ranking is on dashboard 01.

**Column orientation:** bath readings come from the `preset_*` columns and setpoints from `actual_*`, because the source swaps the two names for bath temperatures only. `actual_copperplating1` holds steady within a lot while `preset_copperplating1` moves many times per lot, the signature of a setpoint and a reading. Pump and current columns are not swapped. One setpoint row serves both banks because `preset_current` of side a equals side b on every row.

**Units:** the card uses three tiers of units.

- **Given by the source:** `line_speed` m/min, `density` ASD (A/dm²), `plating_area_a/b` dm².
- **Proven from the data:**
  - `width × height` is in mm, because `plating_area_a` = (height/100) × (width/100) to two decimals on nearly every row.
  - `plating_time` is in minutes, because `plating_time × line_speed` lands within ±0.2 of 54 on nearly every row.
- **Not given and not provable:** `thickness` and `frequency_1` are shown as recorded, with no unit. `frequency_1` is `preset_frequency_1`, and the source stores the same value in `actual_frequency_1` and `pump_frequency`. It is not confirmed to be the Cu frequency on the machine screen.

**What the machine screen has and this panel does not, because the source has no column for it:**

- Part No. `jobkey` mixes lot numbers, part-like codes and test jobs, so it is never labelled Part or Lot.
- Wave No. There is only the `waveform` name, often empty and shown as *not specified*.
- Yield pcs and Empty jig.
- Robot settings.
- Per-station panel size. `width`, `height` and `thickness` are one value per row.
- Pass or fail device checks. `current_check` and `frequency_check` are mode codes (0, 1, and a rare OK), not results.

**Lines, not machine names:** the machines were renamed on 2026-09-11 (`VCP002-VCP` became `VCP02-VCP`). Each card reads the newest row of either name, so the rows from before the rename belong to the same line.

**Reading size:**
- **Sizes:** rectifier amperes are 15 px at every width, hero numbers 21 px, bath readings 15 px and labels at least 10 px.
- **Height:** the panel is 29 grid rows (1,094 px), so the whole overview fits one screen at 1,400 to 1,920 px wide.
- **Width:** the rectifier matrix uses the full panel width, about 95 px per station at 1,920 px.

-- LOCAL: the setting ends with this query and never rides on to the next
-- query that reuses the pooled connection
SET LOCAL jit = off;
WITH incident_alarm AS (
    -- a code that re-fires within 30 minutes on the same machine is the same incident
    -- still standing: most Triggered rows are re-fires of an open incident
    SELECT *, (log_date - LAG(log_date) OVER (
                 PARTITION BY equipment_id, error_code, error_type, alarm_status
                 ORDER BY log_date, log_id) >= interval '30 minutes'
               OR LAG(log_date) OVER (
                 PARTITION BY equipment_id, error_code, error_type, alarm_status
                 ORDER BY log_date, log_id) IS NULL) AS is_incident
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_alarm
    -- bound the window to the panel's range plus one incident gap, so the LAG runs
    -- over a slice rather than the whole table
    WHERE log_date >= $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - interval '30 minutes'
      AND log_date <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz
),
latest_upp AS (
    -- one card per physical line: the newest row of either name is the line's
    -- reading. One backward probe of the log_date index per line; sorting every
    -- wide row of the history to keep one per line spilled 65 MB per worker
    SELECT u.*
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) AS code
          FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel) c
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT x.*,
               -- the bank is plating when any of its 36 sides draws current
               (COALESCE(x.actual_current_1a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_1b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_2a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_2b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_3a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_3b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_4a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_4b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_5a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_5b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_6a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_6b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_7a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_7b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_8a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_8b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_9a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_9b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_10a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_10b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_11a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_11b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_12a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_12b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_13a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_13b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_14a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_14b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_15a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_15b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_16a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_16b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_17a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_17b, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_18a, 0) + COALESCE(x.actual_current_18b, 0)) AS bank_amps
        FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp x
        WHERE x.log_date <= to_timestamp(${__to} / 1000.0)
          AND x.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP'
          AND right(split_part(x.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) = c.code
          AND x.factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
        ORDER BY x.log_date DESC, x.log_id DESC
        LIMIT 1
    ) u
),
latest_status AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2)) right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS line, s.equipment_id, s.current_status, s.log_date as status_time
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_status_change s
    WHERE s.factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (s.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
      AND s.log_date <= to_timestamp(${__to} / 1000.0)
    ORDER BY right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2), s.log_date DESC, s.log_id DESC
),
active_alarms AS (
    SELECT right(split_part(a.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS line, COUNT(*) as alarm_count,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.error_type = 'ALARM') AS alarm_crit,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.error_type = 'Warning') AS alarm_warn
    FROM incident_alarm a
    WHERE $__timeFilter(a.log_date)
      AND a.alarm_status = 'Triggered' AND a.is_incident
      AND a.error_type IN (${severity:sqlstring})
      AND a.factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (a.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(a.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
    GROUP BY 1
),
alarm_recent AS (
    -- four newest triggers per line, read straight off the (equipment_id, log_date DESC) index
    SELECT right(split_part(u.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS line, r.equipment_id, r.log_date, r.error_code, r.error_msg, r.error_type, r.rn,
           u.log_date AS data_at
    FROM latest_upp u CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT al.equipment_id, al.log_date, al.error_code, al.error_msg, al.error_type,
               row_number() OVER (ORDER BY al.log_date DESC, al.log_id DESC) AS rn
        FROM public.eap_api_vcp_alarm al
        WHERE al.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(al.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) = right(split_part(u.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AND al.alarm_status = 'Triggered'
          AND $__timeFilter(al.log_date)
          AND al.error_type IN (${severity:sqlstring})
        ORDER BY al.log_date DESC, al.log_id DESC LIMIT 4
    ) r
),
alarm_cleared AS (
    -- the first Reset of the same code at or after the trigger closes it out
    SELECT r.*, c.log_date AS reset_at,
           EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (c.log_date - r.log_date)) AS open_s
    FROM alarm_recent r
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT z.log_date FROM public.eap_api_vcp_alarm z
        WHERE z.equipment_id = r.equipment_id AND z.error_code = r.error_code
          AND z.alarm_status = 'Reset' AND z.log_date >= r.log_date
          AND z.log_date <= to_timestamp(${__to} / 1000.0)
        ORDER BY z.log_date ASC LIMIT 1
    ) c ON true
),
alarm_flat AS (
    SELECT line,
           MAX(to_char(log_date AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok','HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS at1,
           MAX(error_code) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS code1,
           MAX(error_msg) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS msg1,
           MAX(error_type) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS type1,
           MAX(CASE WHEN reset_at IS NULL AND data_at <= log_date THEN 'open · after the newest data row'
                    WHEN reset_at IS NULL THEN 'open ≥ ' || CASE WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 60 THEN floor(GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0))::int::text || ' s'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 3600 THEN round((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 60.0)::int::text || ' min'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 86400 THEN round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' h'
                  ELSE round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' d' END
                    WHEN open_s < 60 THEN floor(open_s)::int::text || ' s'
                    ELSE ROUND((open_s/60.0)::numeric,1)::text || ' min' END) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS dur1,
           MAX(to_char(reset_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok', 'HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=1) AS rel1,
           MAX(to_char(log_date AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok','HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS at2,
           MAX(error_code) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS code2,
           MAX(error_msg) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS msg2,
           MAX(error_type) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS type2,
           MAX(CASE WHEN reset_at IS NULL AND data_at <= log_date THEN 'open · after the newest data row'
                    WHEN reset_at IS NULL THEN 'open ≥ ' || CASE WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 60 THEN floor(GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0))::int::text || ' s'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 3600 THEN round((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 60.0)::int::text || ' min'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 86400 THEN round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' h'
                  ELSE round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' d' END
                    WHEN open_s < 60 THEN floor(open_s)::int::text || ' s'
                    ELSE ROUND((open_s/60.0)::numeric,1)::text || ' min' END) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS dur2,
           MAX(to_char(reset_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok', 'HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=2) AS rel2,
           MAX(to_char(log_date AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok','HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS at3,
           MAX(error_code) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS code3,
           MAX(error_msg) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS msg3,
           MAX(error_type) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS type3,
           MAX(CASE WHEN reset_at IS NULL AND data_at <= log_date THEN 'open · after the newest data row'
                    WHEN reset_at IS NULL THEN 'open ≥ ' || CASE WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 60 THEN floor(GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0))::int::text || ' s'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 3600 THEN round((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 60.0)::int::text || ' min'
                  WHEN (GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) < 86400 THEN round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' h'
                  ELSE round(((GREATEST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (data_at - log_date)), 0)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1)::text || ' d' END
                    WHEN open_s < 60 THEN floor(open_s)::int::text || ' s'
                    ELSE ROUND((open_s/60.0)::numeric,1)::text || ' min' END) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS dur3,
           MAX(to_char(reset_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok', 'HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=3) AS rel3,
           MAX(to_char(log_date AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok','HH24:MI:SS')) FILTER (WHERE rn=4) AS at4,
           MAX(error_code) FILTER (WHERE rn=4) AS code4,
           MAX(error_msg) FILTER (WHERE rn=4) AS msg4,
           MAX(error_type) FILTER (WHERE rn=4) AS type4,

panels.title: Plating Current by Station
panels.description:
**Use it when:** you need to know which station carries more or less load than its neighbours, before changing a recipe or checking contacts.

**How to read it:** one bar per station, 01 to 18 in the order the panel travels. The value is the **mean plating current in amperes**, not a difference, so it is never negative. Bar colour is the line. The two machine names of one line (for example `VCP002-VCP` and `VCP02-VCP`) are one bar. A bar clearly shorter than its neighbours is a station carrying unusually little load.

**Calculated from:** `actual_current_*a` of all 18 stations in `eap_api_vcp_upp`, averaged over rows where that station draws more than 0 A. Rows where the line is not plating record 0 and would drag the mean down until it means nothing.

**Abnormal when:** one station is far below both neighbours while every station has a similar setpoint. A whole line low at once is usually the recipe or panel size, not a station.

**What to do next:** compare with "Cell Voltage by Station" next to it. Low current with high voltage points to a contact or anode. To see how far a station is from its setpoint, open dashboard 01 panel "Current Deviation by Station", which plots the signed difference.

**Good to know:** side b is not plotted because `actual_current` of the two sides almost never differs. The per-side difference is in the voltage, shown in the next panel. Every selected line is shown, not only the one drawing the most current.

WITH agg AS (
    -- One grouped pass over the window; the unpivot runs on the 18 aggregates
    -- afterwards rather than on every row. Grouped by physical line so both
    -- name eras pool into one bar: grouping by equipment_id but labelling by
    -- line gave two rows per bar and the matrix pivot silently kept one.
    SELECT 'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS line,
           AVG(actual_current_1a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_1a > 0) AS c1,
           AVG(actual_current_2a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_2a > 0) AS c2,
           AVG(actual_current_3a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_3a > 0) AS c3,
           AVG(actual_current_4a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_4a > 0) AS c4,
           AVG(actual_current_5a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_5a > 0) AS c5,
           AVG(actual_current_6a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_6a > 0) AS c6,
           AVG(actual_current_7a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_7a > 0) AS c7,
           AVG(actual_current_8a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_8a > 0) AS c8,
           AVG(actual_current_9a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_9a > 0) AS c9,
           AVG(actual_current_10a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_10a > 0) AS c10,
           AVG(actual_current_11a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_11a > 0) AS c11,
           AVG(actual_current_12a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_12a > 0) AS c12,
           AVG(actual_current_13a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_13a > 0) AS c13,
           AVG(actual_current_14a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_14a > 0) AS c14,
           AVG(actual_current_15a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_15a > 0) AS c15,
           AVG(actual_current_16a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_16a > 0) AS c16,
           AVG(actual_current_17a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_17a > 0) AS c17,
           AVG(actual_current_18a) FILTER (WHERE actual_current_18a > 0) AS c18
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp
    WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
      AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 'Stn ' || LPAD(v.num::text, 2, '0') AS "station",
       a.line AS "line",
       ROUND(v.amp::numeric, 0) AS "actual_current (A)"
FROM agg a
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES
           (1, a.c1),
           (2, a.c2),
           (3, a.c3),
           (4, a.c4),
           (5, a.c5),
           (6, a.c6),
           (7, a.c7),
           (8, a.c8),
           (9, a.c9),
           (10, a.c10),
           (11, a.c11),
           (12, a.c12),
           (13, a.c13),
           (14, a.c14),
           (15, a.c15),
           (16, a.c16),
           (17, a.c17),
           (18, a.c18)
) AS v(num, amp)
ORDER BY v.num, 2;

panels.title: Cell Voltage by Station
panels.description:
**Use it when:** the current matches the recipe but the plated surface is still uneven. That is usually cell resistance, not the recipe.

**How to read it:** one group of bars per station, split by line and side (for example `VCP02 a`, `VCP02 b`). Side a is blue and side b light blue. The value is the **mean cell voltage in volts**, not a difference, so it is never negative. At equal current, the higher side is the one with more resistance.

**Calculated from:** `actual_voltage_*a` and `actual_voltage_*b`, averaged over rows where that side draws current (`actual_current` of the same side above 0), because voltage with no current means nothing. Averaged per line, with both machine names of a line as one line. Averaging all lines together would hide an abnormal cell of one line (one line needs several times the volts per amp of the others).

**Abnormal when:** the two sides of one station clearly differ at equal current, or one station is higher than the whole bank.

**What to do next:** open dashboard 01 panel "Cell Resistance Deviation" for the percentage against the bank median, then take the cell number to the floor to check contacts and anode.

**Good to know:** `actual_voltage` of side a and side b often differs, unlike `actual_current`, which almost never does. A cell that needs more voltage than its neighbours at equal current has a contact or anode with more resistance. No spec band is drawn because the table has no voltage-limit column.

panels.title: Bath Temperature, 7 Steps
panels.description:
**Use it when:** watching, while the line runs, whether all seven bath steps hold their usual level.

**How to read it:** one line per bath, in the order the panel travels. The value is the **temperature the sensor reads, in °C**, not a difference, so it is never negative. The one exception is the dashed *prep setpoint* line: prep has no reading column. A line drifting away from where it used to sit is the bath to check.

**Calculated from:** `eap_api_vcp_upp`, averaged per time bucket at the resolution of the selected window. Read from the `preset_*` columns, which hold the reading, The dashed line is `actual_prep`, the only prep column, which holds one fixed value per line on every row, so it is the recipe setpoint, not a reading.

**Abnormal when:** a line shifts level and stays there for the whole shift, not just a swing, or the two copper baths move in opposite directions.

**What to do next:** open dashboard 01 panel "Bath Deviation from Setpoint", which plots the signed difference from setpoint and is covered by two alert rules, then check which lots were affected in "Recipe Compliance by Lot".

**Good to know:** `preset_*` columns hold the sensor reading and `actual_*` the recipe setpoint, because the source swaps the two names. `preset_dry` has many distinct values and moves within every lot; `actual_dry` has only a handful and holds through the lot. A `preset_dry` of 0 means no reading, not a cold dryer.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(log_date, $__interval),
       ROUND(AVG(preset_clean)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_clean",
       ROUND(AVG(actual_prep)::numeric, 1) AS "actual_prep",
       ROUND(AVG(preset_copperplating1)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_copperplating1",
       ROUND(AVG(preset_copperplating2)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_copperplating2",
       ROUND(AVG(preset_ao)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_ao",
       ROUND(AVG(preset_hotwater)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_hotwater",
       ROUND(AVG(preset_dry)::numeric, 1) AS "preset_dry"
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
  AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Line Speed & Current Density
panels.description:
**Use it when:** you change the line speed and want to see the current density at the same moment.

**How to read it:** the left axis is `line_speed` in m/min and the right axis is `density` in A/dm² (ASD), one line per plating line. Both are read straight from their columns and are never negative.

**Calculated from:** `line_speed` and `density` in `eap_api_vcp_upp`, averaged per time bucket and line. Read straight from the columns, not recomputed.

**Abnormal when:** one of the two changes with no lot change behind it. Both are recipe values, so a change outside a lot change means a value was not updated by the machine.

**What to do next:** check whether the jobkey on the card above changed at that moment. If the job did not change but the value did, look at "Machine State Timeline" for a stop at that time.

**Good to know:** `density` is not `actual_current` divided by area; no combination of columns reproduces it, so the column is shown as recorded. **The two lines do not move together:** `density` and `line_speed` are practically uncorrelated on every line. The right axis is there to see both on one screen, not because one drives the other. **Both are recipe values, not continuous measurements:** each line uses only a short list of `density` and `line_speed` values, and most lots keep one of each for the whole lot. Steps in the lines are **recipe or lot changes**, not process swings. `density` and `line_speed` are not recorded as 0, so a gap in the graph means no rows in that time, not a stopped line.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 
    $__timeGroupAlias(log_date, $__interval),
    'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) || ' · line_speed' AS metric,
    ROUND(AVG(line_speed)::numeric, 2) AS value
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
  AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT 
    $__timeGroupAlias(log_date, $__interval),
    'VCP' || right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) || ' · density' AS metric,
    ROUND(AVG(density)::numeric, 2) AS value
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
  AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Machine State Timeline
panels.description:
**Use it when:** looking back at when a machine stopped and for how long, before comparing with the alarms below.

**How to read it:** one band per line. The colour is the value `current_status` actually holds, not a number derived from it. The length of a segment is the time spent in that state. Every line's first segment starts at the left edge of the window, because the state before the window is carried in.

**Calculated from:** `eap_api_vcp_status_change`: the latest state before the selected range heads the timeline, followed by every state change inside it.

**Abnormal when:** a DOWN or ALARM segment runs for hours, or the state flips unusually often, which usually comes with the same alarm code firing again and again.

**What to do next:** note when the stop began, then read "Alarm Log" below at the same time to find which code came first. For the whole week, open dashboard 01 panel "Hours by State".

**Good to know:** states are not turned into numbers, because RUN=2, IDLE=1, rest=0 would merge DOWN, ALARM and PM into one band. Over 180 days `current_status` holds RUN, DOWN, IDLE, ALARM and PM; STOP appears only in `previous_status`. **The vertical event lines (annotations) are off by default.** Turn them on with the "Left RUN" and "ALARM before a stop" switches at the top of the dashboard. They are off because a month holds hundreds of exits from RUN, and the dashed lines would cover the graph. The same exits show in this timeline as segment edges.

**Lines that stop sending data:** a line's band ends 5 minutes after its last data row, followed by a grey NO DATA segment to the end of the window, instead of stretching the last state as if the line were still running. This matches how "Hours by State" counts hours. The state in force when the window opens is read from both names of the line.

targets.rawSql:
WITH initial_state AS (
    -- the state standing when the window opened, from either name of the line
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (right(split_part(s0.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2)) right(split_part(s0.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS code,
           $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AS log_date, current_status
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_status_change s0
    WHERE s0.log_date <= $__timeFrom()::timestamptz
      AND s0.log_date > $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - interval '30 days'
      AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
    -- qualified: the output column above is also called log_date, and an
    -- unqualified ORDER BY would sort by that constant and pick a random state
    ORDER BY right(split_part(s0.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2), s0.log_date DESC, s0.log_id DESC
), silent AS (
    -- the moment each line stopped reporting telemetry; the bar ends there with
    -- NO DATA instead of stretching the last state to the edge of the window
    SELECT right(split_part(u.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS code,
           GREATEST(max(u.log_date) + interval '5 minutes', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz) AS log_date
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_upp u
    WHERE u.log_date <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz
      AND u.log_date > $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - interval '30 days'
      AND u.factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (u.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(u.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
    GROUP BY 1
), window_changes AS (
    SELECT right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) AS code, s.log_date, s.current_status
    FROM public.eap_api_vcp_status_change s
    LEFT JOIN silent x ON x.code = right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2)
    WHERE $__timeFilter(s.log_date)
      AND s.factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
      AND (s.equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(s.equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
      AND (x.log_date IS NULL OR s.log_date < x.log_date)
), combined AS (
    SELECT code, log_date, current_status FROM initial_state
    WHERE current_status = ANY(ARRAY[${status_filter:sqlstring}])
    UNION ALL
    SELECT code, log_date, current_status FROM window_changes
    WHERE current_status = ANY(ARRAY[${status_filter:sqlstring}])
    UNION ALL
    SELECT code, log_date, 'NO DATA' FROM silent
    WHERE log_date < $__timeTo()::timestamptz
)
SELECT log_date AS "time",
       'VCP' || code AS "metric",
       current_status AS "value"
FROM combined
ORDER BY 2, 1;

panels.title: Alarm Log
panels.description:
**Use it when:** an alarm has gone off and you need to know at once which code, which machine, and whether it has cleared.

**How to read it:** one row per log row from the machine, not merged, so a code that re-fires every few minutes shows every time. The KPI panels and the live cards count incidents instead (a code re-firing within 30 minutes counts once), so the two counts differ on purpose. Newest first. `alarm_status` Triggered means it just fired; Reset means it cleared. `error_type` is the severity as the source records it, ALARM or Warning, and the filter above sets which ones show. Column headers are the database column names, unchanged and untranslated, so a row can be matched to the database exactly.

**Calculated from:** `eap_api_vcp_alarm` for the selected range, line and `error_type`, sorted by `log_date` newest first, and capped at 100 rows so the panel stays fast on a wide range.

**Abnormal when:** the same code shows Triggered again with no Reset in between, or many Triggered rows arrive close together from one line.

**What to do next:** click a row to open dashboard 01 for that line, then check "Alarm Codes Preceding Stops" for how often this code has been followed by a stop, before deciding whether to stop the line or run on.

**Good to know:** the table has only two `error_type` values, ALARM and Warning (far more common), each with similar numbers of Triggered and Reset rows. The 100-row cap means a wide range does not show every older event; narrow the window to look further back.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_char(log_date AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Bangkok', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS "log_date",
       equipment_id AS "equipment_id",
       error_type AS "error_type",
       COALESCE(error_code, '-') AS "error_code",
       error_msg AS "error_msg",
       COALESCE(alarm_status, '-') AS "alarm_status"
FROM public.eap_api_vcp_alarm a
WHERE $__timeFilter(log_date)
  AND factory IN (${factory:sqlstring})
  AND (equipment_id LIKE '%-VCP' AND right(split_part(equipment_id, '-', 1), 2) IN (SELECT right(split_part(sel, '-', 1), 2) FROM unnest(ARRAY[${equipment_id:sqlstring}]) AS sel))
  AND error_type IN (${severity:sqlstring})
-- a.log_date, not the formatted text column of the same name (whole seconds)
ORDER BY a.log_date DESC, a.log_id DESC
LIMIT 100;
